T-statistics of intraspecific trait variation

Source: R/individuals.R
tstats.Rd

Computes the three variance ratios of Violle et al. (2012) for each site (community) and trait, from trait values of individuals such as those of sample_individuals():

Usage

tstats(
  individuals,
  traits = "trait",
  site = "site",
  species = "species",
  method = c("base", "cati"),
  nperm = 99,
  ...
)

Arguments

individuals

Data frame with one row per individual, such as from sample_individuals().

traits

Names of the columns with trait values.

site, species

Names of the columns with the site and the species of each individual.

method

"base" (the default) for the observed values only, or "cati" for cati::Tstats() with null models; it needs the package cati.

nperm

Number of randomisations of the null models of method = "cati"; NULL for observed values only.

...

Further arguments to cati::Tstats(), such as reg.pool or independantTraits.

Value

With method = "base", a data frame with one row per site and trait and the columns site, trait, n_populations, T_IP.IC, T_IC.IR and T_PC.PR; statistics that cannot be computed, such as T_PC.PR for a site with one species, are NA. With method = "cati", the Tstats object of cati::Tstats(), with the site names of individuals, for its methods cati::ses.Tstats(), plot() and summary().

Details

  • T_IP.IC, the mean variance among individuals within the populations of the site over the variance among all individuals of the site. Low values mean that the populations of co-occurring species overlap little (niche differentiation within the community).

  • T_IC.IR, the variance among individuals of the site over that among all individuals of the region. Low values mean that the site holds a narrow part of the regional trait range (environmental filtering of individuals).

  • T_PC.PR, the variance among population means within the site over that among all population means of the region. Low values mean filtering of populations.

A population is a species at a site. Variances use n - 1, means of the variances within populations are not weighted, and populations of a single individual have no variance and are left out of T_IP.IC, as in cati::Tstats().

method = "base" computes the observed values in base R, with no null model. It is fast and needs no other package, which suits simulation studies with many replicates, where the truth is known and each statistic is compared among scenarios rather than with a null model. method = "cati" calls cati::Tstats() (Taudiere & Violle 2016), which adds null models: individuals permuted within each site for T_IP.IC, individuals drawn from the regional pool for T_IC.IR, and population means permuted for T_PC.PR. Both give the same observed values. cati::Tstats() finds the populations of a site by matching its name as a regular expression, so a site called site1 would also take the populations of site10; the sites are therefore passed under labels of equal width (site01, site02, ...) and given back their names in the result.

Local adaptation

With local_adaptation in sample_individuals(), population means move toward the environment of their site, so co-occurring species become more alike and the region spreads along the environment. The variance among populations within a site falls, so T_PC.PR and T_IC.IR fall, and T_IP.IC rises, because the populations that remain overlap more. A fall in T_IP.IC with local adaptation would need populations to diverge from co-occurring species, as in character displacement, which sample_individuals() does not simulate.

References

Taudiere, A., & Violle, C. (2016). cati: an R package using functional traits to detect and quantify multi-level community assembly processes. Ecography, 39, 699–708. doi:10.1111/ecog.01433

Violle, C., Enquist, B. J., McGill, B. J., Jiang, L., Albert, C. H., Hulshof, C., Jung, V., & Messier, J. (2012). The return of the variance: intraspecific variability in community ecology. Trends in Ecology & Evolution, 27, 244–252. doi:10.1016/j.tree.2011.11.014

See also

sample_individuals().

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(landscape_implicit(15), species_traits(tree),
                              competition_matrix(tree, "none"), n_steps = 100,
                              seed_steps = 1:5)
none <- tstats(sample_individuals(sim, intraspecific_sd = 2))
local <- tstats(sample_individuals(sim, local_adaptation = 0.8, intraspecific_sd = 2))
colMeans(none[, c("T_IP.IC", "T_IC.IR", "T_PC.PR")], na.rm = TRUE)
#>    T_IP.IC    T_IC.IR    T_PC.PR 
#> 0.02299744 0.89106250 1.11059919 
colMeans(local[, c("T_IP.IC", "T_IC.IR", "T_PC.PR")], na.rm = TRUE)
#>    T_IP.IC    T_IC.IR    T_PC.PR 
#> 0.33914930 0.03219661 0.03057455 
# with the null models of cati; ses.Tstats() lists T_IP.IC, T_IC.IR and T_PC.PR in order
res <- tstats(sample_individuals(sim, intraspecific_sd = 2), method = "cati", nperm = 19)
round(cati::ses.Tstats(res)[[1]]$ses[, 1], 1)
#>  site1  site2  site3  site4  site5  site6  site7  site8  site9 site10 site11 
#>  -15.6  -12.9  -16.9  -13.9   -8.7  -10.7   -8.7  -16.9   -7.1  -11.7  -14.8 
#> site12 site13 site14 site15 
#>  -11.2  -15.1  -10.2  -18.5
